reviewer: builder (the agent session that wrote the generator)
findings: Five storeys: a ground storey and four ribbon and band pairs on all four sides, as both perspective references show.
Each band reads as a main face under a projecting cap strip with a dark reveal line 0.16 m tall; the first band carries a lower moulding.
Ribbons read as continuous dark strips; columns stand 1.5 m back and corner rooms have their blinds drawn, so no sight line runs through a corner.
The walkway mouth is closed by solid jambs and full-height frame posts; its glass sits 0.11 m behind the tube face.
Roof plan matches the reference in footprint ratio, penthouse position, the rear east well, the walkway position and the roof items.
The entrance is a pair of glazed doors in the second bay from the east corner with a glazed draught lobby behind; the threshold is 35 mm above grade.
West flank and rear are complete service elevations with real openings; both are inferred and recorded as such.
Nothing floats and nothing sits below grade. Every swept piece faces outward, which a test now checks piece by piece.
changes_since_v002: Every finding of the independent review of v002 was acted on in v005, which then passed independent review. v006 acts on eight of the nine P2 notes from that pass; see evidence/independent-review-v005.json.
open_notes: The street reference shows far more penthouse above the parapet than the roof plan and oblique allow, so the model's street skyline is flatter. Recorded as a source conflict; roof plan governs.
The walkway is a 9 m length with a glazed end and no support at the free end; the references run it to a neighbouring building.
Both perspective references place the walkway at the third storey, not the second where a +15 normally sits. Built as drawn.
Joints 30 mm wide break up into dashes in distant views, and shadow edges under the soffit are stepped in close views. Both come from the review renderer, not the geometry.
